doc.headline: Keep {arm:September}: both candidates hold Kairo in character less often, and at this run's unnamed provider routing both also cost more per reply.
doc.lede: {arm:qwen3.8-flash}'s character pass rate is clearly lower than {arm:September}'s and {arm:1017}'s drop is not told apart from zero, so neither beats the control on what was asked. Only a candidate that kept character better would change the call; a named provider pricing one below {arm:September} would remove the cost half of the reason, not the character half.

caveats.material_if: Only if the judge marks the candidates' replies down for style rather than character. Then the call would rest on cost alone, which is measured at a routing no arm names and which an earlier round contradicted for {arm:qwen3.8-flash}; it would hold only as the status-quo default until the costs are repriced.

caveats.label: Costs belong to an unnamed provider routing
caveats.material_if: Only if a named provider prices a candidate at or below {arm:September}. Then the cost half of the call falls and it rests on character, where {arm:qwen3.8-flash} is still clearly worse and {arm:1017} is not shown better.
Only if a different character aspect would have been chosen before the results, and that aspect showed a candidate ahead of {arm:September}.
Only if the intended baseline was not the model in production today; {arm:September} is that model.
Only if some setting besides the model moved between arms; each arm's recorded settings change the model alone.

decision.text: Keep {arm:September} (the control) as Kairo's persona model. Its character pass rate is {pass_rate.September}, the highest of the three, at {cost_per_1k.September|usd_per_1k} production cost, the lowest of the three at this run's routing, which no arm names.

{arm:qwen3.8-flash}: its character pass rate is down {reading.qwen3.8-flash.change|abs|pts} points (interval {reading.qwen3.8-flash.interval|interval}) and at this run's routing it costs {contrast.qwen3.8-flash.production_replicating_cost.delta|abs|usd_per_1k} more. {arm:1017}: its pass-rate drop of {reading.1017.change|abs|pts} points is not told apart from zero, it holds character less often by {contrast.1017.persona.holds_character.delta|abs|pts} points, and at this run's routing it costs {contrast.1017.production_replicating_cost.delta|abs|usd_per_1k} more.

The weakest margin is {weakest.arm}'s pass rate against the margin on character adherence: its family-corrected interval reaches {weakest.value|pts} against a line at {weakest.threshold|pts}, {weakest.margin|abs|pts} points short of it; on the {reading.qwen3.8-flash.level} reading its drop reaches {flip_margin.qwen3.8-flash|abs|pts} points, the figure the margin control uses. Neither moves the call, since {arm:September} is kept either way. This run contradicts the earlier finding that {arm:qwen3.8-flash} lowers production cost; no arm names its provider, so whether the routing changed is unknown. {arm:1017} spent {reasoning_ratio.1017} of its output reasoning against {reasoning_ratio.September} for {arm:September}, so its figures are not at matched reasoning.

Keep {arm:September} now. Rework how every model handles off-lane asks, where both candidates fall furthest behind, and rerun all three arms; in parallel, calibrate the judge and reprice the arms at named providers.

claims.text: Both candidates hold Kairo in character less often than {arm:September}: {arm:qwen3.8-flash} is clearly worse on the character pass rate, by {contrast.qwen3.8-flash.passed.delta|abs|pts} points, and {arm:1017} is down {contrast.1017.passed.delta|abs|pts} points, not told apart from zero, while the judged holds-character rate is lower for both. Each drop stays inside the declared {aspects.character adherence (v2).margin|int}-point margin.

evidence.caption: Change against {arm:September} on the character pass rate and the judged holds-character rate, paired over {contrast.qwen3.8-flash.passed.n_cases|int} cases, at the family-corrected {family.level} level; the shaded band is the margin. {arm:1017} reasoned on a smaller share of its output than {arm:September}, which could pull its character figures either way; {arm:qwen3.8-flash} lost {scoreboard.qwen3.8-flash.lost|words} trials to the harness, too few to move its rate.

claims.text: At this run's routing, which no arm names, both candidates cost more to run: {arm:qwen3.8-flash} by {contrast.qwen3.8-flash.production_replicating_cost.delta|abs|usd_per_1k} and {arm:1017} by {contrast.1017.production_replicating_cost.delta|abs|usd_per_1k}, each interval clear of zero.

evidence.caption: Paired production-cost gap against {arm:September}, at the family-corrected {family.level} level. Some trials reported no cost ({cost.unreported.September.missing|int} for {arm:September}, {cost.unreported.qwen3.8-flash.missing|int} for {arm:qwen3.8-flash}, {cost.unreported.1017.missing|int} for {arm:1017}). Filling {arm:September}'s at its own p95 puts its mean at {cost.unreported.September.at_p95|usd_per_1k}; counting the candidates' as free puts theirs at {cost.unreported.qwen3.8-flash.free|usd_per_1k} and {cost.unreported.1017.free|usd_per_1k}, so the order holds even at that worst case. {arm:1017} reasons less than {arm:September}; matching its reasoning would likely widen its cost gap.

claims.text: Off-lane asks are where both candidates fall furthest behind on the judged holds-character rate ({strata.off_lane.qwen3.8-flash.persona.holds_character.vs_control|pts} points for {arm:qwen3.8-flash}, {strata.off_lane.1017.persona.holds_character.vs_control|pts} for {arm:1017}), and where {arm:September} is weakest too among strata of ten cases or more, at {strata.off_lane.September.persona.holds_character.mean}.

evidence.caption: Each candidate's judged holds-character rate minus {arm:September}'s, in the eight largest strata; uncorrected and exploratory, so read the off-lane gap as a lead. {arm:1017}'s rows carry its lower reasoning share, which could move them either way.
Each arm's judged holds-character rate on off-lane asks, over {strata.off_lane.n_cases|int} cases.

claims.text: Read from the few off-lane failures the snapshot kept, they fall into two patterns: brushing the ask off in voice and then slipping out of it (the first and third cards, from {arm:1017} and {arm:September}), and answering the non-music request that should have been declined (the second card, from {arm:qwen3.8-flash}). Among the other kept failures, answering the ask appears for all three models, so neither pattern belongs to one model alone.

evidence.caption: One kept off-lane failure per arm, the control's among them. The snapshot kept {count.examples.character adherence (v2).September.off_lane|words} of {count.failures.character adherence (v2).September.off_lane|int} off-lane failures for {arm:September}, {count.examples.character adherence (v2).qwen3.8-flash.off_lane|words} of {count.failures.character adherence (v2).qwen3.8-flash.off_lane|int} for {arm:qwen3.8-flash} and {count.examples.character adherence (v2).1017.off_lane|words} of {count.failures.character adherence (v2).1017.off_lane|int} for {arm:1017}, so the patterns are a reading of a sample, not a count.

method.text: {cases|int} cases, each run {repeats|words} times per arm; intervals count cases, not trials.

Readings against the control are at {reading.qwen3.8-flash.level}. Contrasts are paired over cases and corrected together by Holm's method across {family.family_size|int} comparisons, each interval at {family.level}. The weakest margin is read on the corrected interval, the margin control on the readings. Stratum breakdowns are uncorrected.

A candidate may be up to {aspects.character adherence (v2).margin|int} points worse on the character pass rate and still count as acceptable; set after the results, and the call holds at every margin.
The floor on the rate drop reads the character pass rate for {arm:qwen3.8-flash} but the judged holds-character rate for {arm:1017}, a mismatch; both held, and the call rests on neither floor.
One model judged every dimension, with no calibration ratings, so its tier is undetermined.

Production cost per 1,000 replies, replicating what production pays; no arm names its provider, so the routing behind each cost is unknown and the cost order is this run's, not the models' own. Token counts and model-call counts were not reported.
Latency, because every run executed beside others. Whether the simulated user's request settings varied was not recorded on every run.

findings.finding: The lede and the cost caveat's clause both say that repricing a candidate below September would remove only 'the cost half' and leave the call standing, because qwen3.8-flash is 'still clearly worse' on character. But under the declared 15-point margin, both candidates count as acceptable on character: qwen3.8-flash's worst drop is 10.8 and 1017's is 5.8. So if one were cheaper, which is what the earlier round found for qwen3.8-flash, September would no longer beat it on every axis. The question would become a declared trade: up to about 7.6 points of character for the saving. The page currently reads as if repricing cannot reopen the call. Fix: in the lede and the cost-routing clause, say that a cheaper candidate inside the margin would turn the call into a character-for-cost trade under the declared criteria. Then say either that you would still keep September, and why the 15-point margin should not govern, or that the repricing next step could change the recommendation.

items.name: First screen
items.reason: The headline and decision block give a clear call (keep September), the reasons (character and cost) and a Watch line. But half of the reason is cost, and the headline and the recommendation ('the lowest production cost of the three') present cost as something the model itself does. In fact the costs come from a provider routing nobody named, and an earlier round found qwen3.8-flash cheaper. That qualifier only appears further down, in Watch and in claim cost.

items.name: Coherent story
items.reason: The claims follow from one another, and each sentence matches its values table: in claim character, A's pass rate is -7.6 (-12.59 to -2.57), B's is -3.0 (-7.36 to +1.34), and both holds-character rows are clear of zero. Two loose ends: Watch puts A's headroom against the margin at 2.4 points on the corrected interval, while 'What you could change' says A's verdict turns at a 10.8 margin, which implies 4.2 points of room. And claim off-lane calls off-lane September's weakest stratum, though the full table shows 'assistant shape' lower at 58.8% (only 6 cases).

items.name: Honest emphasis
items.reason: September's weak spot is shown (65.8% on off-lane asks), and B's pass-rate drop is correctly called not told apart from zero. But the confidence clauses for the judge caveat and the late-aspect caveat fall back on the production-cost gap as 'measured and does not rest on the judge'. They don't say that the gap belongs to an unnamed routing that an earlier round contradicted. So the fallback reads firmer than it is.

items.name: Sound elision
items.reason: None of the omitted items would change the call. The outcome and transcript scores go the same way as the character finding. The booth, delivery and failed-reply measures are not separated for either candidate. Measuring spend is also higher for both candidates ($6.28 and $5.76 against $5.40), so it agrees with the cost story.

items.name: Confounds handled
items.reason: The reasoning-share confound on 1017 (55% against 76%) is carried in claim character, claim cost, Watch and the next steps, and unknown routing has its own next step. But claim off-lane reads 1017's holds-character drop (-4.7, -8.2 to -1.3), which the reasoning confound attaches to, and neither the claim nor the confidence carries it.

items.name: Actionable next steps
items.reason: Each step names an experiment and what it would settle: rework off-lane handling and rerun, calibrate the judge, confirm routing and reprice, and rerun 1017 at matched reasoning. The 815-cases figure matches the settle arithmetic (80% power). It doesn't say that the suite holds only 299 cases.

items.name: Evidence fits claims
items.reason: Claim off-lane's own figures (loss shares of 48% and 53%, and September's 65.8% off-lane rate) are not in its block, which draws only per-stratum deltas. Claim cost's caption calls $2.02 September's 'p95', but September's p95 is $5.30 per 1,000 replies. $2.02 is September's mean with its 33 trials that reported no cost filled in at that p95, and the candidates' '$2.24' and '$2.36' are their means with uncosted trials set to zero.

findings.finding: The page ranks the models by cost without naming a provider. The headline ('both candidates cost more per reply'), the recommendation ('the lowest production cost of the three') and two confidence clauses (judge, late aspect) treat the cost gaps (+$0.62 and +$0.49 per 1,000 replies) as properties of the models and as the firm fallback if the judge is wrong. No arm names its provider, and Watch says an earlier round found qwen3.8-flash cheaper. Fix: in the headline and the decision, say these costs are at this run's unnamed routing. Rewrite the judge and late-aspect clauses so they don't present the cost gap as settled, or name the routing caveat and the earlier contrary finding there and say the call holds as the status-quo default until repricing (next step 3).

Three fixes here. (1) Carry the reasoning-share confound: the claim reads 1017's holds-character drop (-4.7, -8.2 to -1.3), which that confound touches. (2) Put the claim's own figures in the block: the off-lane loss shares (48% for qwen3.8-flash, 53% for 1017) and September's 65.8%. Right now the block shows only the deltas (-22.9 and -20.2). (3) Change 'where September is weakest' to 'weakest among the larger strata', since 'assistant shape' is lower at 58.8% (6 cases).

The caption says 'September (P) at its own p95 ($2.02 per 1,000 replies)', but September's p95 is $5.30. $2.02 is September's mean cost with its 33 trials that reported no cost filled in at its p95, and $2.24 and $2.36 are the candidates' means with their uncosted trials counted as zero. Describe it that way, as a worst-case fill of the missing costs, so a reader doesn't take $2.02 for a per-reply p95.

Watch and 'What you could change' measure qwen3.8-flash's headroom on different interval levels. Watch says 2.4 points short of the 15-point line on the corrected interval (-12.6). The table says its verdict turns at a margin of 10.8, which is the 95% reading and gives 4.2 points of room. State both on one basis, or say which level each one uses.

Next step 4 asks for 815 cases per arm (2,445 trials at three repeats), but the suite has 299 cases. Say that the step needs about 516 new cases, or rephrase it as more repeats, which would not shrink an interval that counts cases.

items.name: First screen
items.reason: The headline, decision block and lead claim say what to do (keep September), why (qwen3.8-flash's pass rate is clearly lower at -7.6 points, -12.6 to -2.6; 1017 is not shown better), and the main risks: the uncalibrated judge, and costs from a routing no arm names, which an earlier round contradicted. The cost half is now tied to this run's routing everywhere it appears.

items.name: Coherent story
items.reason: Each sentence matches its block's rows. In the lead claim, every drop is inside the 15-point line: the lowest end is -12.59 for qwen3.8-flash's pass rate. 1017's pass rate crosses zero (-7.36 to +1.34), and both holds-character drops are separated. In the off-lane claim, -22.9 and -20.2 are each candidate's largest gap in the bars, and September's 65.8% is its lowest among strata of ten cases or more (multi is 72.2%). The cost claim's worst-case fills ($2.02 against $2.24 and $2.36) do keep the order.

items.name: Honest emphasis
items.reason: The page names the recommended arm's open risks: costs at an unnamed routing, the contrary earlier finding, an uncalibrated judge, and 1017's lower reasoning share. It doesn't oversell 1017's 3-point pass-rate drop. The High confidence spells out, clause by clause, what would make each open caveat matter, and says the call holds only as the status-quo default if the judge is wrong.

items.name: Sound elision
items.reason: None of the omitted items changes the call. options_dominance finds September dominant under the declared criteria. Measures that are not separated stay not separated, and 1017's small nonsignificant gains (outcome +0.014, booth offstage +0.8 points) are visible in the appendix. Dropping the off-lane loss shares only removes a derived figure.

items.name: Confounds handled
items.reason: The reasoning-share confound (1017 at 55% against September's 76%) is carried on every claim that reads 1017, including the off-lane claim, and into next step 4. The model confound is the comparison itself, and the page says so. Both late criteria are checked: decision_sensitivity on the margin keeps September at every margin, with flips at 5.8 for 1017 and 10.8 for qwen3.8-flash and neither changing the call. qwen3.8-flash's two harness-lost trials are noted.

items.name: Actionable next steps
items.reason: Each step names an experiment and what it settles: rework the off-lane directive and rerun, calibrate the judge against human ratings, reprice the arms at named providers, and rerun 1017 at matched reasoning on 815 cases. The last step now says new cases must be written and that more repeats would not help.

items.name: Evidence fits claims
items.reason: The lead forest shows both measures with the margin line. The cost forest shows the gap. The off-lane claim now carries September's 65.8% and the candidates' rates in its own table. The cost caption now describes the $2.02 figure correctly. One soft spot is in the cards claim (see finding).

findings.finding: The cards claim says off-lane failures 'look alike across all three models', then describes two different patterns: cards 1 and 3 brush the ask off and then slip out of voice, while card 2 answers the non-music request. It also generalises from three kept examples per arm, against 39, 64 and 62 failures. The snapshot's kept failures show the 'answers the ask' pattern in more than one model (for example, 1017's jeans-wash reply that gives 'Cold'). Fix: say the kept off-lane failures fall into two patterns, brushing off and then slipping, and answering the ask; say both appear in more than one model; and say this is read from the few failures the snapshot kept.

items.name: First screen

On the reason: qwen3.8-flash's pass rate is down 7.6 points (95% interval -10.8 to -3.4), 1017's 3-point drop is not told apart from zero but its holds-character rate is down 4.7, and both cost more at this run's routing. items.name: Coherent story

items.name: Honest emphasis

The cost gap is always tied to an unnamed routing. Watch names the weakest margin (-12.6 against -15) and 1017's lower reasoning share (55% vs 76%).

The small strata (assistant shape, next up) show smaller drops than off lane, and the page names assistant shape. Latency is properly excluded because runs executed concurrently.
